_comment: st_dd0e19d8 AC4 — every publication path the repository documents or scripts, enumerated,
so 'publishing happens through the checked step or it does not happen' can be CHECKED rather
than believed. scripts/qa/publication-paths-proof.js re-derives the candidate set from the
tree on every run and refuses when a candidate is missing from this file, when an entry names
a file that no longer exists, or when a file listed as removed is still present.
The derivation is DATA, not a rule buried in the proof: `signals` below are the literals that
make a file a candidate. A new script that pushes, adds a remote, creates a repository, or
archives a tree matches one of them and forces a decision. Widening the signal list is how the
enumeration keeps up with the repository; narrowing it is how someone would hide a path, which
is why the list lives here in the open next to the classifications it drives.
checked-step   the one step that may publish. Performs the push itself.
routes-through the file participates in publication but only through the checked step.
not-a-path     matches a signal but cannot publish this repository. Reason required.
removed        a publication path this story deleted. The proof asserts it is really gone.

exclude_from_derivation.reason: npm lockfile — dependency metadata, never executed
generated file inventory; it names every script by path and would match on any signal any script contains

paths.reason: the sequence of refusals ending in the only push. Requires --from <named commit>, checks the destination, proves detection, audits the built tree, and only then pushes.
the checked step's logic. Exposes pushExportTree, which publish() reaches only after every refusal above it has passed.
builds a throwaway export to prove the composed scans detect inside it. Adds no remote and never pushes; the directory is deleted in a finally.
pushes a marketing SITE repository under the configured sites root, resolved per finding by _repoRootForFiles, which returns null for any file outside it. It cannot address this repository.
a comment describing the export-tree signature it refuses to build a corpus from. No git invocation.
a comment explaining why gitignored overrides never reach an export. No git invocation.
documentation of git filter-repo recovery steps for the development repository. Prose, not a path.

this file. It declares the signals, so it necessarily contains them. Enumerated rather than excluded from the derivation: an exclusion is a file nobody has to justify, and the whole point of this list is that every match is justified.
the proof itself. It reads the signals and greps for an executed push, so it carries both. Same reasoning as the file above — named and classified, not hidden behind an exclusion.

builds throwaway export trees to demonstrate each refusal. Its git runner throws on any push argv, so a future edit that reached the push step during a probe fails loudly instead of publishing. This entry exists because the proof caught the file the moment it was written — which is the enumeration working.
a comment noting the AC2 baseline is extracted with git archive into a scratch directory, read-only, with no worktree or branch mutation. No remote, no push.
a comment naming the export-tree signature under test.
a comment stating the test clones rather than archives, because it needs a working .git.
asserts the gsc-heal push stays explicit opt-in. A test of a guard, not a path.
asserts the qa skill still calls git push for ordinary development commits to the private repository.

removed.reason: the previous publication path. It built from `git stash create` (working-tree state, not a named commit), ran two composed scans that were structural no-ops inside the export, and left the push to a human — moving the one irreversible action outside the checks. Deleted rather than kept as a shim: a second way to publish is a second way to publish unchecked.
